display.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the Holy Neshamah
display.summary_short: A couple's child, born through the Baal Shem Tov's blessing, dies at two. The Baal Shem Tov reveals whose holy soul it was, and the mitzvos with young children that brought them a new son.
display.summary_long: The storyteller first traces a family link: the Tzemach Tzedek's stepmother was the daughter of Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, and this is the story of how Rabbi Aharon was born. He reads the Frierdiker Rebbe's note that the story teaches the merit of saying Amen and Kedushah with small children and of training babies in mitzvos. A hidden tzaddik's wife receives the Baal Shem Tov's blessing and has a beautiful boy, but at two, after the Baal Shem Tov blesses and kisses him, the child passes away. The Baal Shem Tov tells the grieving parents a parable: a holy soul volunteered to be born as a king's son to save the Jews from a decree, grew up to discover that his teacher, the Pope, was secretly a Jew, and himself became a ger. Its only flaw was that it had nursed for two years from a non-Jewish mother, and their child had been that soul, sent back to fix it. He tells the father to become a shammes who says Amen with children and lifts them to kiss the Sefer Torah, and the mother to help poor new mothers and teach babies' mitzvos. Two years later Aharon is born. The storyteller ends with the Alter Rebbe's seven lessons from the story.
display.lesson: Saying Amen, brachos and Kedushah with little children, and training even babies in mitzvos, carries great merit; good deeds by both parents awaken Heavenly mercy.
